name: The Spine
design_intent:
THE SPINE — the max-exposure sky-ridge (v1_level_circuit.md §L-5, build order #2). The deliberate COUNTERWEIGHT to drop_chamber's enclosure: where the drum SEALS you in (edges save, centre kills), the Spine strips ALL cover — one long thin ridge hangs in open sky with a bottomless void on BOTH long sides AND directly below the entire length. There is almost no safe interior: the void floor sits right under the whole thin ridge, so a knock from ANYWHERE on it (down or outward off the thin strip) is a potential ring-out. This is the level where the edge-kill fantasy is at its purest — the recovery gamble (fuelled fly-back along the ridge) IS the whole game. Kill-shape class = void_is_floor -> QA uses K1' (off-screen kills >= 88%, uncredited self-falls <= 12%), NOT the central_pit K1 edge/pit ratio (docs/specs/v2a_kill_shape_void_floor_addendum.md §3); a high void/pit share here is the fantasy working, not a regression.

DISTINCT FROM the two prior islands-over-void levels: islands_void is an even ARCHIPELAGO of four WIDE (960px) landing islands with forgiving runway; the Spine is the inverse — ONE central thin ridge (no wide safe top) plus two small SPRING perches out at the very brink of the void (620px out, only ~500px inside the side blast) and one high throne. drop_chamber is an enclosed bumper drum; the Spine is total open-sky exposure. Feel = 'everything happens on the edge of the abyss.'

ENGINE RISK: NONE new. Reuses the islands-over-void static-geometry physics + the pit_void_rendering void treatment (which now draws a proper chasm under any floating platform and in the gaps between them, via paint_void(platform_rects)). No new primitive; no Tuning/lethality/feel constant touched (fence per v1_level_circuit.md §6 — GEOMETRY + theme only).

GEOMETRY: central RIDGE (trampoline, x0..1500, top y880, thin h56) is the home strip. Two small SPRING perches flank it at ridge height OUT over the void — LEFT x-900..-620 (620px gap from the ridge's left end at x0) / RIGHT x2120..2400 (620px gap from the ridge's right end at x1500). One central SPRING throne x580..920 top y360 hangs 520px ABOVE the ridge top (boost-only). ONE full-width lethal void runs under the whole span (rim y960, a dark bottomless chasm). Bounds -1400..2900 keep the two perches' outer edges only ~500px inside the side blast lines (the 'ends sit just inside blast range', §L-5) so falling off a perch outward is a fast side/void ring-out, while the bottom bound (y1660) leaves 724px of recovery sky under the ridge.

MOVEMENT-TOOL-PER-GAP ANALYSIS (Tuning.gd: trampoline apex 270px / bubblegum 180 / spring 480; air_drift_max 340px/s, gravity 1600 => zero-boost horizontal reach ~395px off a trampoline, ~527px off a spring; normal_boost_max 760px/s crosses a 620px gap in <0.9s @ ~24 fuel, bounce refunds +20; super_boost_impulse 2800 clears everything but dumps the tank):
- REACH the LEFT perch: ridge left end x0 to perch right edge x-620 = 620px of open void. > 527 (max spring drift, and the launch surface is the trampoline ridge at ~395 drift, so >> 395) and there is no spring on the ridge to drift further. NORMAL BOOST REQUIRED; a bounce-hop drifts at most ~395px and drops into the void. Verb: FLY. (Rule A, >= 560.)
- REACH the RIGHT perch: ridge right end x1500 to perch left edge x2120 = 620px over the void. > 527. NORMAL BOOST REQUIRED; miss = fall into the void. Verb: FLY. (Rule A.)
- RETURN from a perch: the perch springs launch you 480px up but the 620px gap back to the ridge still exceeds the 527 spring drift, so even leaving a perch needs a boost — flight is required BOTH directions (no bounce route exists across the level). Verb: FLY.
- CLIMB to the central THRONE (top y360): 520px above the ridge top (y880). The best ridge bounce is the trampoline apex 270 -> only reaches y610, 250px short; no spring sits on the ridge. JETPACK CLIMB REQUIRED; an under-shot climb drops back to the thin ridge or past it into the void. Verb: FLY. (Rule B, >= 500.)
- SUPER as the committed play: a full super clears a 620px perch gap or the throne climb in one blast (contest the throne, snipe a rival off a perch into the void) but drains the tank -> the committed cross-map play, not routine traversal. Verb: FLY+SMASH. (Rule C.)
- RECOVER after being knocked off the ridge: the drop from the ridge bottom (y936) to the bottom blast line (y1660) is 724px of open sky over the chasm (>= 650, Rule D) -> a healthy fuelled player who is knocked outward off the thin ridge can boost back along the ridge (the recovery gamble that IS this level), while a near-brink dead-on smash or a starved/damaged victim rings out. The perches sit only ~500px inside the side blast, so a knock off a perch OUTWARD is a much shorter, less recoverable ring-out (the perches are exposed prizes). Verb: FLY.
- Every crossing (620px perch gap) exceeds even a spring bounce's 527px reach and far exceeds the trampoline ridge's ~395px drift, and the throne sits 520px above the ridge (> the 480 spring apex), so NO route across or up the arena exists without the jetpack. The thin ridge gives NO wide safe runway (unlike islands_void's 960px islands), so a launched player rarely re-lands on it -> the highest kill-per-exchange in the circuit (SP1). Vertical AND horizontal distance are load-bearing, not scenery.

SUCCESS CRITERIA (void_is_floor class, §L-5): SP1 — because the whole thin surface is near-edge, credited off-screen kills >= 90% and near-edge dead-on hits ring out >= 8/10 (highest kill-per-exchange). SP2 — a mid-ridge healthy full-fuel player knocked outward flies back >= 5/10 (intentionally lower than the roomier levels' ~8/10 because this is THE exposed level, but never 0/10; if < 4/10 the ridge is WIDENED, never the lethality touched). SP3 — flight-required: perch reach needs a boost >= 9/10 (zero-boost falls short into the void). VOID READS AS DEATH via the pit_void_rendering treatment (dark cool bottomless gradient + receding dirt canyon walls at the ridge/perch cliffs + under-lip AO + matte hazard-red rim/chevrons along y960 + falling motes) so the whole underside of the ridge is unmistakably lethal, not safe green sky.
